questions.q: What does running EXEC sp_configure with no parameters do?
options: Lists current server configuration option values
Immediately restarts the SQL Server instance
Deletes all custom configuration
Rebuilds every index on the instance
questions.explain: sp_configure with no arguments displays the current configuration options and their values.

questions.q: What must you run after changing an sp_configure value for the change to take effect?
options: RECONFIGURE
REBUILD
REFRESH
COMMIT
questions.explain: RECONFIGURE applies a pending sp_configure change; some options also require a restart before the run_value matches the config_value.

questions.q: Why does Microsoft hide most sp_configure options behind 'show advanced options' by default?
options: Most advanced options can hurt performance if changed without understanding the tradeoff, so the visibility gate discourages casual changes
Advanced options are deprecated and no longer functional
They are hidden for licensing reasons tied to edition
Hidden options only apply to Azure SQL Database, never on-prem
questions.explain: Turning on show advanced options doesn't change server behavior itself — it only controls what a later sp_configure listing displays.

questions.q: What does the remote query timeout option control?
options: How many seconds a query against a remote data source, such as through a linked server, waits before timing out
How long a local T-SQL query can run before being killed
How long a backup operation can run before being cancelled
How long a login attempt waits before failing
questions.explain: Its default is 600 seconds; a value of 0 means wait indefinitely, which can let a hung remote call tie up local resources indefinitely too.

questions.q: What tradeoff does lowering an index's fill factor below the default involve?
options: Fewer page splits from future inserts/updates, at the cost of more disk space and more pages to scan
Faster backups with no other effect
Guaranteed elimination of all future page splits with no downside
It only affects clustered indexes, never nonclustered ones
questions.explain: A lower fill factor leaves free space on each page deliberately, reducing page splits on write-heavy indexes but increasing the index's total size.
